answer: Sybil resistance requires each verified identity to complete a prescribed, non-parallelizable sequence of modular squarings: every square depends on the preceding result, so GPUs cannot divide one proof’s chain into concurrent work. An attacker may create clones, but each must still endure the full sequential delay and produce a valid Wesolowski proof, imposing a strict physical time bottleneck. Like a garden in a gale, a dependent vine cannot grow faster by adding workers.
